# Music API v2

> HTTP JSON API and web remote for Spotify. It controls playback on a real speaker, searches the Spotify catalog, manages playlists and the user's library, reads listening history, and adds synced lyrics (LRCLIB) and the host machine's audio mixer. Base URL: https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org

This file is the complete reference for driving the API with no other context. It follows the llms.txt convention: the short index is at https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org/llms.txt and the same content as this file is at /LLMS.md. Everything here was written from the server's source code (server.py, player.py, spotify.py, extras.py, soloist.py, tokens.py).

Contents: 1 Basics, 2 Data shapes, 3 Endpoints, 4 Server-sent events, 5 Workflows, 6 Limits and gotchas, 7 Errors, 8 Deployment.

---

## 1. Basics

### Base URL

- Public: `https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org` (a Cloudflare tunnel to the server on `127.0.0.1:8765`).
- On the host machine itself: `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

The examples below use:

```sh
API=https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org
TOKEN=mapi_...   # ask the user for one
```

### Authentication

Send the API token on every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer mapi_...
```

or, where headers can't be set (browser `EventSource`, `<img src>`, links), as a query parameter: `?token=mapi_...`.

A token is required for everything except:

- `GET /` and any other non-`/api` page (the web app; it shows a Slack sign-in screen when needed)
- `GET /auth/slack/login`, `GET /auth/slack/callback`, `POST /auth/slack/logout` (Sign in with Slack)
- `POST /slack/commands`, `POST /slack/interactions`, `POST /slack/events` (the Slack bot; called by Slack only, each request must carry a valid `X-Slack-Signature` for `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`, else 401)
- `GET /llms.txt`, `GET /llms-full.txt`, `GET /LLMS.md`, `GET /API.md`, `GET /README.md`
- `GET /auth/callback` (protected by the OAuth PKCE state instead)
- `OPTIONS` (CORS preflight)

The public server runs with `--public`, so a token is required even for requests from localhost. Missing or wrong token: `401 {"error": "unauthorized"}`.

There are no scopes: every token can do everything, including creating and revoking other tokens. See "Tokens" in section 3.

The web app instead uses a session cookie from Sign in with Slack (pinewoodrobotics workspace only). Sessions belong to a person: non-admin sessions get `403 {"error": "admins only"}` on tokens, the Spotify login, `/api/spotify/*`, `/api/library/*`, `/api/recent`, `/api/top`, `/api/me`, `/api/devices/transfer`, the raw `GET/POST /api/playlists` list, and hidden playlists. API tokens act as the user **Admin** and can do everything. `GET /api/app/me` says who you are.

Do not confuse the API token with the Spotify Web API login. They are separate. The server holds one Spotify login (the account whose music this is); you never send Spotify credentials. If the Spotify login is missing or expired, Web API endpoints fail with 412 and an error text that mentions `/auth/login` (see section 7). A 401 always means a missing or wrong API token.

### Requests

- Bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`). `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` is also accepted. An empty body is fine where every field is optional.
- Query strings carry `limit`, `offset`, `q` and so on.
- CORS: every response has `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; preflight allows GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and the `Content-Type` and `Authorization` headers.
- Trailing slashes are ignored. Unknown path: `404 {"error": "not found"}`. Known path, wrong method: `405 {"error": "method not allowed"}`.

### Response envelope

Success: HTTP 200 with

```json
{"result": <any JSON value>}
```

Failure: HTTP 4xx/5xx with

```json
{"error": "human-readable message"}
```

Exceptions to the envelope:

- `GET /api` returns a bare JSON array (no `result` wrapper).
- `GET /api/artwork` returns `302` with a `Location` header, or raw image bytes with `?proxy=1`.
- `GET /auth/login` returns an HTML page (or `302` to Spotify with `?redirect=1`); `/auth/callback` returns HTML.
- `GET /api/events` is a `text/event-stream`.
- The documentation files are `text/plain` or `text/markdown`.

### IDs, URIs and links

Spotify identifies things by a 22-character base62 ID and a URI of the form `spotify:<type>:<id>`, where type is one of `track`, `album`, `playlist`, `artist`, `episode`, `show`, `audiobook`, `chapter`.

Where each form is accepted:

| Place | Bare ID | `spotify:` URI | open.spotify.com link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Path parameters (`/api/albums/{id}`, `/api/playlists/{id}`, ...) | yes (required) | no | no |
| `/api/tracks/{id}` | yes, or the word `current` | PATCH only | no |
| `/api/play` `uri`, `context`; `/api/play-url` `url` | no | yes | yes |
| `/api/play` `uris[]`, `offset` (as URI) | yes (treated as a track) | yes | yes |
| `/api/queue` `uri` / `uris[]` | yes (treated as a track) | yes | yes |
| `/api/lyrics?track=` | yes (track) | yes | yes |
| `uris` for library and playlist-items endpoints | no | yes | yes |

Links may include `intl-xx/` or `embed/` path segments and query strings such as `?si=...`; they are normalized to URIs. Every object the API returns carries both `uri` and `id`, so the simplest rule is: pass `uri` in bodies, `id` in paths.

### Pagination

List endpoints return a page object (section 2). Use `limit` and `offset`. `next` is a boolean that tells you whether there are more. Default `limit` is 20 and the cap is 50 unless noted (search: max 10). Followed artists use a cursor instead (`after`).

---

## 2. Data shapes

The API returns compact objects, not Spotify's raw ones.

Track:

```json
{"uri": "spotify:track:4uLU6hMCjMI75M1A2tKUQC", "id": "4uLU6hMCjMI75M1A2tKUQC", "type": "track",
 "name": "Never Gonna Give You Up",
 "artists": [{"uri": "spotify:artist:0gxyHStUsqpMadRV0Di1Qt", "name": "Rick Astley"}],
 "album": {"uri": "spotify:album:...", "name": "Whenever You Need Somebody"},
 "duration_ms": 213573, "explicit": false, "track_number": 1,
 "artwork": "https://i.scdn.co/image/...", "is_local": false}
```

Episode: `uri, id, type: "episode", name, show: {uri, name}, duration_ms, explicit, release_date, artwork`.

Album: `uri, id, type: "album", name, artists[], album_type, release_date, total_tracks, artwork`.

Artist: `uri, id, type: "artist", name, genres, artwork`.

Playlist: `uri, id, type: "playlist", name, owner` (display name string), `description, public, collaborative, total` (item count), `artwork`.

Show / audiobook: `uri, id, type, name, description, artwork`.

When the current item comes from the Soloist backend (section 6), tracks have `uri, id, type, name, duration_ms, explicit, artwork, album: {uri, name}, artists[]` (no `track_number` or `is_local`).

Page:

```json
{"items": [ ...objects... ], "total": 123, "offset": 0, "limit": 20, "next": true}
```

Rows from the library, history and playlist items also carry `added_at` or `played_at` (ISO 8601). Items Spotify reports as unavailable (`null`) are dropped, so `items` can be shorter than `limit`.

Status (`GET /api/status`, and the `status` SSE event):

```json
{"backend": "connect", "state": "playing", "active": true,
 "device": {"id": "...", "name": "Lab Mac", "type": "Computer", "active": true, "supports_volume": true},
 "position_ms": 61234, "position": 61.234, "duration_ms": 213573, "volume": 65,
 "shuffle": false, "repeat": "off",
 "track": { ...track or episode, or null... },
 "context": {"uri": "spotify:playlist:...", "type": "playlist"},
 "actions": [],
 "credit": {"by": {"id": "U123", "name": "Ada", "avatar": "https://..."}, "how": "queued"}}
```

- `state`: `playing`, `paused` or `idle` (nothing on any device). Soloist may also report other states such as `buffering`.
- `repeat`: `off`, `context` or `track`.
- `actions`: the actions currently allowed, using Soloist's names (`play`, `pause`, `seek`, `skip_next`, `skip_prev`, `shuffle`, `set_repeat`, `add_to_queue`, plus `seek_forward`/`seek_backward` with Soloist). On the connect backend it's derived from Spotify's `disallows`. It's empty when nothing is playing.
- `source`: where the current track came from: `context`, `queue` or `autoplay` (Soloist only; null if unknown).
- `skip`: for 30 s after someone presses next/previous or jumps in Up Next: `{"by": {id, name, avatar}, "from": <uri of the track they skipped>, "at": unix ms}`, else null. The skip is credited on the track that was skipped; the new track keeps its own `credit`.
- `credit`: who is responsible for the current track, or null. `how` is `queued` (someone added it with `POST /api/queue`) `started` (someone began playback of it or of its album/playlist/artist with `POST /api/play`, `/api/play-url`, `/api/playlists/{id}/play` or Slack), or `autoplay` (Spotify picked it after the album/playlist ended; `by` is `{"id": null, "name": "Autoplay", "avatar": null}`). It stays the same for the whole track and survives restarts; credits expire after 6 hours (queued) or 12 hours (started).
- With the Soloist backend there are also `connected`, `logged_in` and `error` fields, `device` is `{name, type: "Soloist", active}`, and `context` is a compact object (`uri, id, type, name, artwork`).
- When idle (connect backend), `device`, `track`, `context`, `volume`, `shuffle` and `repeat` are null.

---

## 3. Endpoints

Each heading is `METHOD path`. "Body" means a JSON body; "?" marks optional fields. Unless noted, the result is described inside `{"result": ...}`.

Which endpoints need the Spotify Web API login: all of Catalog, Playlists, Library & history, `/api/me`, `/api/lyrics?track=`, `/api/spotify/*`; all playback with the connect backend; and some playback with the Soloist backend (noted below). The playback backend in use is reported by `GET /api/backend`.

### Discovery

#### GET /api
Bare JSON array (no envelope) of `{"method", "path", "doc"}` for every route on the running server. Use it to check what the live server supports.

### Playback

#### GET /api/status
Full status object (section 2), fetched fresh.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $API/api/status
```

#### GET /api/now-playing
Just `status.track`: the current track/episode object, or `null`.

#### POST /api/play
Play or resume. With no body, resumes. Body (all optional):

- `uri`: one URI or link. Tracks and episodes play on their own; albums, playlists, artists and shows start that context.
- `shuffle`: `true`/`false` sets shuffle before playing (the web app's Play button sends `false` so albums start at track 1 in order; Shuffle sends `true`).
- `uris`: list of track/episode URIs (or bare track IDs) to play as an ad-hoc list.
- `context`: album/playlist/artist/show URI, with
- `offset`: where to start in the context, either an integer index (0-based, must be a JSON number) or a track URI/ID.
- `position` (seconds) or `position_ms`: start position.

Returns the status object. A request that names something to play is credited to the caller (`status.credit`); a bare resume isn't.

```sh
# a track
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uri": "spotify:track:4uLU6hMCjMI75M1A2tKUQC"}' $API/api/play
# an album, starting at its 3rd track
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"context": "spotify:album:6N9PS4QXF1D0OWPk0Sxtb4", "offset": 2}' $API/api/play
# resume
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $API/api/play
```

#### POST /api/play-url
Body `{url}`: play any open.spotify.com link or `spotify:` URI. Same as `/api/play` with `{uri: url}`.

#### POST /api/pause
Pause. Returns status.

#### POST /api/playpause
Toggle: pauses if playing or buffering, otherwise resumes. Returns status.

#### POST /api/next
Skip to the next item. Returns status.

#### POST /api/previous
Previous track. Spotify restarts the current track instead if it's past the first few seconds. Returns status.

#### POST /api/back
Alias of `/api/previous` (kept for v1 clients).

#### POST /api/seek
Body, one of: `{position: seconds}`, `{position_ms}`, `{delta: ±seconds}` (relative). Clamped at 0. Returns status.

#### POST /api/volume
Spotify's playback volume. Body `{volume: 0-100}` or `{delta: ±n}`. Clamped to 0-100. Returns status. Some Connect devices (e.g. phones) don't support remote volume; check `status.device.supports_volume`. For the host machine's own speaker volume, see `/api/system/volume`.

#### POST /api/shuffle
Body `{enabled?: bool}`. Omit `enabled` to toggle. Returns status.

#### POST /api/repeat
Body `{mode?: "off"|"context"|"track"}`. `one` = track, `all` = context, `none` = off are accepted. Omit to cycle off → context → track → off. Returns status.

#### GET /api/artwork
Cover art of the current item. Default: `302` redirect to Spotify's image CDN. `?proxy=1`: the image bytes themselves (cached, `Cache-Control: max-age=3600`), for clients without HTTPS. `404` if nothing is playing. Needs the token like everything else, so use `?token=` in an `<img>` tag.

#### GET /api/lyrics
Lyrics for the current song, from lrclib.net. Optional `?track=<id|uri|link>` for any other track (needs the Web API).

```json
{"source": "lrclib.net", "instrumental": false,
 "synced": [{"time_ms": 18230, "text": "We're no strangers to love"}, ...],
 "plain": "We're no strangers to love\n...",
 "match": {"track": "...", "artist": "...", "album": "..."},
 "track": {"uri": "spotify:track:...", "name": "..."},
 "position_ms": 61234, "line": 7}
```

- `synced` is empty when only plain lyrics exist; `plain` can be null.
- `line` is the index into `synced` of the line being sung now (`-1` before the first line). `position_ms` and `line` are only present for the current song, not with `?track=`.
- `instrumental: true` means there are no words.
- `404` when nothing is playing, for podcast episodes ("lyrics are only available for songs"), or when LRCLIB has nothing ("no lyrics found"). Lookup is exact (title, artist, album, duration) with a fuzzy search fallback; check `match` if it looks wrong.

#### GET /api/sleep
Sleep timer: `{"active": false}` or `{"active": true, "ends_at": <unix seconds>, "remaining": <seconds>, "fade": <seconds>}`.

#### POST /api/sleep
Body `{minutes, fade?}`: pause after `minutes` (may be fractional), fading the volume out over the last `fade` seconds (default 30). After pausing, the volume is restored to its earlier level so the next play isn't silent. Setting a new timer replaces the old one. Returns the sleep status.

#### DELETE /api/sleep
Cancel the timer (restores volume if a fade had started). Returns the sleep status.

### Activity feed

#### GET /api/activity
What people did in the last 24 hours, oldest first: `{"entries": [...], "latest": <id>}`. `?since=<id>` returns only entries with a higher id (poll or catch up after reconnecting); without it you get the newest `limit` entries. `?limit=` defaults to and is capped at 500. Open to every signed-in user, not admin-only. The same entries are pushed live as the `activity` SSE event (section 4).

Entry: `{"id": 42, "at": 1760000000000, "by": {"id", "name", "avatar"}, "action": "queue_add", "detail": {...}, "origin": "web"}`. `id` increases monotonically; `at` is unix milliseconds. `origin` is `web` (session cookie), `api` (API token), `media-session` (request header `X-Client-Origin` starting with `media-session`, i.e. the OS media controls) or `slack` (the bot's buttons and `/music` commands).

Only successful actions are recorded. Names can arrive late: the entry is first sent with URIs only, then sent again with the same `id` and `names`/`name` filled in, so replace by `id`. `volume` entries coalesce: the same person changing volume again within 10 s updates that entry (new `at` and `volume`, same `id`); so do `playlist_reorder` entries for the same person and playlist.

| `action` | `detail` |
|---|---|
| `play`, `pause` | `{}` (`POST /api/playpause` records whichever it did) |
| `play_item` | `{uri, type, name?}` of what was started |
| `next`, `previous` | `{from?}`: name of the track that was playing |
| `jump` | `{name?}`: the Up Next track jumped to |
| `seek` | `{position_ms}` |
| `volume` | `{volume}` |
| `shuffle` | `{enabled}` |
| `repeat` | `{mode}`: `off`, `context` or `track` |
| `queue_add` | `{uris, count, names?}` |
| `playlist_create` | `{id, name}` |
| `playlist_import` | `{id, name, imported, source}` |
| `playlist_rename` | `{id, name}` (new name) |
| `playlist_delete` | `{id, name}` |
| `playlist_add` | `{id, count, name?, names?}` |
| `playlist_remove` | `{id, count, name?}` |
| `playlist_play` | `{id, name?}` |
| `playlist_duplicate` | `{id, name, from}`: the new playlist and the id it was copied from |
| `playlist_reorder` | `{id, name?}` |
| `album_add`, `album_remove` | `{id, name}` of a Library album (`name` can be null on remove) |
| `library_songs_play` | `{uri, name, count}`: song the Library list was started from and how many tracks were queued |

### Queue and devices

#### GET /api/queue
`?limit=n` optional.

- connect backend: `{"current": <item>, "upcoming": [{"uid": null, "source": null, "item": <item>}], "previous": []}`.
- Soloist backend: `{"upcoming": [...], "previous": [...]}`, each `{"uid", "source", "item"}` where `source` is `context`, `queue` or `autoplay`; up to 80 upcoming.
- Upcoming entries also carry `added_by`: `{"id", "name", "avatar"}` of whoever queued that track through this API in the last 6 hours, else null.

#### POST /api/queue/jump
Body `{uid}` (from `GET /api/queue`, Soloist) or `{index}` (0 = the next entry): skip ahead to that Up Next entry, dropping the entries before it, like clicking a song in Spotify's queue. 409 if that uid is no longer in Up Next. Returns the status.

#### POST /api/queue
Body `{uri}` or `{uris: [...]}`: add tracks or episodes to the end of the user queue (bare IDs are treated as tracks). Albums and playlists can't be queued; play them, or queue their tracks one by one. Returns `{"added": [uris]}`.

#### GET /api/devices
Spotify Connect devices on the account: `[{"id", "name", "type", "active", "volume", "restricted"}]`. With the Soloist backend each also has `soloist: bool`, and the Soloist device is always listed. Without a Web API login the list is empty (connect backend).

#### POST /api/devices/transfer
Body `{device, play?}`: move playback to a device. `device` is a device `id` or its `name` (case-insensitive) from `/api/devices` (or `"soloist"`). `play: true` starts playing there; otherwise the current play/pause state is kept. Returns `{"transferred": <device>}` (or status, for Soloist). `404` if the device isn't found or online.

#### GET /api/backend
```json
{"backend": "connect",
 "web_api": {"configured": true, "logged_in": true, "scope": "...", "redirect_uri": "...", "expires_at": 1760000000},
 "soloist": {"connected": true, "endpoint": ["127.0.0.1", 9999], "data_dir": "...", "error": null,
             "logged_in": true, "is_active": true, "device_name": "Lab Speakers"}}
```
`soloist` is present only with the Soloist backend.

#### POST /api/backend/soloist/{verb}
`verb` = `activate` or `deactivate`: make the Soloist device the active Spotify device, or release it. `404` without the Soloist backend. Returns status.

### Catalog (needs the Web API)

#### GET /api/search
Query: `q` (required), `type` (comma-separated from `track,album,artist,playlist,show,episode,audiobook`; default `track,album,artist,playlist`), `limit` (default and max 10), `offset`.

Result: an object keyed by the plural type, each a page: `{"tracks": page, "albums": page, ...}`. Spotify search syntax works in `q`, e.g. `track:"Clocks" artist:Coldplay`, `year:1990-1999`, `genre:jazz`.

```sh
curl -s -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $API/api/search \
  --data-urlencode 'q=never gonna give you up' -d type=track -d limit=3
```

#### GET /api/tracks/{id}
One track, plus `saved: bool` (in Liked Songs). `id` may be `current`.

#### PATCH /api/tracks/{id}
Body `{saved: bool}`: add to or remove from Liked Songs. `id` may be `current`, a bare ID, URI or link. Returns `{"uri", "saved"}`.

#### GET /api/albums/{id}
Album plus `label` and `tracks` (first page; each track has `album` and `artwork` filled in).

#### GET /api/albums/{id}/tracks
`?limit=&offset=`. Page of tracks.

#### GET /api/artists/{id}
One artist.

#### GET /api/artists/{id}/albums
`?include_groups=album,single,appears_on,compilation&limit=&offset=`. Page of albums.

#### GET /api/episodes/{id}
Podcast episode plus `description` and `resume_point`.

#### GET /api/shows/{id}
Podcast plus `episodes` (first page).

#### GET /api/shows/{id}/episodes
`?limit=&offset=`. Page of episodes.

#### GET /api/audiobooks/{id}
Audiobook plus `authors`, `narrators` (name lists) and `chapters` (first page).

#### GET /api/audiobooks/{id}/chapters
`?limit=&offset=`. Page of chapters.

#### GET /api/chapters/{id}
One audiobook chapter.

### Playlists (needs the Web API)

#### GET /api/playlists
The user's playlists (owned and followed). `?limit=&offset=`. Page of playlist objects. `owner` is the owner's display name; compare with `GET /api/me` `name` to find playlists you can edit.

#### POST /api/playlists
Body `{name, description?, public?, collaborative?}`. Creates a playlist owned by the logged-in user. Returns the playlist object. Spotify sometimes ignores `public` on create; the server re-applies it and returns what Spotify actually stored.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Robotics build night", "public": false}' $API/api/playlists
```

#### GET /api/playlists/{id}
Playlist details with `total` item count (no items).

#### PATCH /api/playlists/{id}
Body `{name?, description?, public?, collaborative?}`. Returns the updated playlist.

#### DELETE /api/playlists/{id}
Removes the playlist from the user's library (unfollow). Spotify has no hard delete; for your own playlist this is how deletion works. Returns `{"removed": uri}`.

#### GET /api/playlists/{id}/items
`?limit=` (default and max 50) `&offset=`. Page of tracks/episodes with `added_at`. Spotify only returns items for playlists the user owns or collaborates on; others fail (typically 403/404).

#### POST /api/playlists/{id}/items
Body `{uris: [...], position?: n}` (URIs or links). Appends, or inserts at `position`. Returns Spotify's `{"snapshot_id": ...}`.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"uris": ["spotify:track:4uLU6hMCjMI75M1A2tKUQC"]}' $API/api/playlists/PLAYLIST_ID/items
```

#### DELETE /api/playlists/{id}/items
Body `{uris: [...]}`. Removes every occurrence of each. Returns `{"snapshot_id": ...}`.

#### PUT /api/playlists/{id}/items
Reorder: body `{range_start, insert_before, range_length?}`. Or replace everything: body `{uris: [...]}`. Returns `{"snapshot_id": ...}`.

#### GET /api/playlists/{id}/image
Cover image list `[{url, height, width}]` as Spotify returns it.

#### PUT /api/playlists/{id}/image
Body `{jpeg_base64}`: base64 JPEG (a `data:image/jpeg;base64,...` URL is fine), max 256 KB. Returns `{"uploaded": true}`.

#### POST /api/playlists/{id}/play
Body `{offset?: index|uri, shuffle?: bool}`. Sets shuffle first if given, then plays the playlist. Works for any playlist, including ones whose items you can't read. Returns status.

### Library and history (needs the Web API)

#### GET /api/library/{kind}
`kind` = `tracks` (Liked Songs), `albums`, `episodes`, `shows`, `audiobooks`, `playlists`, or `artists` (followed). `?limit=&offset=`. Rows for tracks, albums, episodes and shows have `added_at`. For `artists` use `?after=<cursor>` instead of `offset`; the page then has an `after` field with the next cursor (null at the end).

#### GET /api/library/contains
`?uris=uri1,uri2` (comma-separated URIs). Returns `{uri: bool}`.

#### PUT /api/library
Body `{uris: [...]}` (max 40, URIs or links): save tracks, albums, episodes, shows, audiobooks, playlists; follow artists or users. Returns `{"saved": [uris]}`.

#### DELETE /api/library
Body `{uris: [...]}` (max 40): remove or unfollow. Returns `{"removed": [uris]}`.

#### GET /api/recent
Recently played tracks. `?limit=` (max 50) `&before=` or `&after=` (unix milliseconds). Page of tracks with `played_at`, plus a parallel `context` array (the playlist/album each was played from, or null).

#### GET /api/top/{kind}
`kind` = `tracks` or `artists`. `?time_range=short_term|medium_term|long_term&limit=&offset=` (about 4 weeks, 6 months, all time).

#### GET /api/me
The logged-in Spotify user: `{"id", "name", "uri", "artwork"}`.

### Web app (accounts and the shared Library)

These power the web app. With an API token you act as `Admin`.

#### GET /api/app/me
`{"id": "U0123" | "admin", "name": "Adam", "avatar": url | null, "admin": bool, "kind": "slack" | "token"}`. `name` is the Slack display name.

#### GET /api/app/token, POST /api/app/token/regenerate
Your personal API token: `{"token": "mapu_...", "created", "docs": "https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org/llms.txt"}`. One per Slack user, created on first request, and it acts as you (same permissions; queued songs and playlists are credited to you). `regenerate` replaces it and the old one stops working immediately. Only for Slack sign-ins (400 when you're using an admin API token).

#### GET /api/app/playlists
The playlists the web app shows: every playlist in the account except the hidden ones (configured on the server), playlists created in the app first (newest first).
```json
[{"id": "...", "uri": "spotify:playlist:...", "name": "Lab bangers", "description": "", "artwork": "https://...", "total": 42,
  "created_by": {"id": "U0123", "name": "Adam", "avatar": "https://..."}, "source_url": "https://open.spotify.com/playlist/..." ,
  "created": "2026-10-09T20:41:00Z", "can_edit": true}]
```
`created_by`, `source_url` and `created` are null for playlists not made through the app. `source_url` is set for imports.

#### POST /api/app/playlists
Body `{name, description?}`. Creates a private playlist on the account, credited to you. Returns the playlist object.

#### POST /api/app/playlists/import
Body `{url}`: a Spotify or Apple Music playlist (or song) link. Copies its tracks into a new playlist credited to you and returns `{"playlist": {...}, "imported": 100, "total": null, "truncated": true, "source": "spotify"|"apple", "unmatched": [{"name", "artists"}]}`. Spotify playlists must be **public** and only the first 100 tracks can be read, so `truncated` just means the cap was hit. 404 if there is no public playlist there.

**Album links are routed to the Library instead** (Spotify `open.spotify.com/album/...` or `spotify:album:`, Apple Music `music.apple.com/.../album/...` without `?i=`): no playlist is created, the album is added as in `POST /api/app/library/albums` and the response is `{"kind": "album", "album": {...album object...}}` (`album.already` is true if it was there already). 422 if an Apple album has no Spotify album match.

#### POST /api/app/playlists/{id}/duplicate
Body `{name?}` (default "<name> (copy)"). Copies the playlist's tracks into a new private playlist credited to you. Returns the new playlist object (`total` = tracks copied). Any signed-in user may duplicate any visible playlist.

#### The Library

The Library is the app's shared playlists plus albums saved as references to the real Spotify album (no copy of the tracks). Albums are stored in `<data-dir>/library-albums.json` (mode 600); album metadata is fetched from Spotify and cached for an hour.

Album object (`kind` is `"album"`; `duration_ms` can be null when the album is long):
```json
{"kind": "album", "id": "1kCHru7uhxBUdzkm4gzRQc", "uri": "spotify:album:1kCHru7uhxBUdzkm4gzRQc", "name": "Hamilton",
 "artists": [{"uri": "spotify:artist:...", "name": "Lin-Manuel Miranda"}], "artwork": "https://...", "total": 46, "year": "2015",
 "duration_ms": 8820000, "added_by": {"id": "U0123", "name": "Adam", "avatar": "https://..."}, "added": "2026-10-09T20:41:00Z",
 "source_url": "https://open.spotify.com/album/...", "can_edit": true}
```
`can_edit` is true for whoever added the album and for admins.

#### GET /api/app/library
`?kind=all|playlists|albums&sort=recent|name|creator` (defaults `all`, `recent` = newest added first; `creator` groups by who added it). Returns `{"items": [...]}`: playlists with the shape of `GET /api/app/playlists` plus `"kind": "playlist"`, and album objects. Playlists not made through the app have no date and sort last under `recent`. `GET /api/app/playlists` still works as before.

#### POST /api/app/library/albums
Body `{url}` or `{uri}`: a Spotify album link/URI, or an Apple Music album link that matches a whole Spotify album. Returns the album object. Idempotent: adding an existing album returns it with `"already": true`. 400 for anything that isn't an album link; 422 (suggesting Import as playlist) when an Apple album has no Spotify album match. Admins may also pass `added_by: {id, name, avatar}` and `added: "<ISO time>"` to credit someone else (used by `deploy/migrate_album_playlists.py`).

#### GET /api/app/library/albums/{id}, DELETE /api/app/library/albums/{id}
`GET` returns the album object plus `"tracks"`: every track as a compact item (`uri, id, name, artists, album, duration_ms, explicit, track_number, artwork`). `DELETE` removes it from the Library (whoever added it, or an admin; else 403) and returns `{"removed": "spotify:album:..."}`. 404 if it isn't in the Library.

#### GET /api/app/library/songs
`?q=&sort=recent|title|artist|album&offset=&limit=` (limit default 100, max 500). Every distinct track across the Library's playlists and albums. `q` matches title, artist or album case-insensitively; `recent` is newest first.
```json
{"items": [{"uri": "spotify:track:...", "id": "...", "type": "track", "name": "Satisfied", "artists": [{"uri": "...", "name": "..."}],
            "album": {"uri": "...", "name": "Hamilton"}, "duration_ms": 331000, "artwork": "https://...",
            "sources": [{"kind": "album", "id": "1kCHru7uhxBUdzkm4gzRQc", "name": "Hamilton"}, {"kind": "playlist", "id": "...", "name": "Lab bangers"}],
            "added": "2026-10-09T20:41:00Z"}],
 "total": 812}
```
`added` is the earliest time the song entered the Library. The aggregated list is cached for about 2 minutes and rebuilt right after any Library change made through this API (adding/removing albums, creating/importing/duplicating/renaming/deleting playlists, adding/removing/reordering playlist tracks). Playlists whose tracks Spotify won't list are skipped.

#### POST /api/app/library/songs/play
Body `{uri, sort?, q?}` (same `sort` and `q` as the songs list). Plays the songs list as an ad-hoc queue (up to 100 tracks, starting at `uri`, in the list's order) and credits you as the starter. 404 if `uri` isn't in the filtered list.

#### GET /api/app/playlists/{id}, PATCH /api/app/playlists/{id}, DELETE /api/app/playlists/{id}
One playlist; `PATCH` body `{name?, description?}`; `DELETE` removes it. Changing or deleting needs `can_edit` (whoever created it, or an admin), else 403. Use `/api/playlists/{id}/items` to list, add, remove and reorder tracks (`PUT` with `{range_start, insert_before, range_length?}`; open to every signed-in user for visible playlists), and `/api/playlists/{id}/play` to play.

### Tokens

Tokens have no scopes; every token is equal and can manage all tokens. Only SHA-256 hashes are stored (in `<data-dir>/api-tokens.json`, mode 600). The plaintext is returned once, at creation, and can never be retrieved again.

#### GET /api/tokens
```json
[{"id": "3f9a1c2e", "name": "kiosk", "prefix": "mapi_Ab3x", "created": 1760000000, "last_used": 1760003600, "current": true}]
```
`prefix` is the first characters of the token, for recognizing it. `current` is true for the token making this request. `created` and `last_used` are unix seconds (`last_used` is updated at most once a minute; null if never used).

#### POST /api/tokens
Body `{name?}` (default name "unnamed"). Returns `{"id", "name", "token", "prefix", "created"}`. Store `token` now; it is shown only this once.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "hallway e-ink display"}' $API/api/tokens
```

#### DELETE /api/tokens/{id}
Revoke immediately. Any token can revoke any token, including itself. Returns `{"revoked": id, "name"}`. `404` for an unknown id. `409` if it's the last remaining token (so nobody gets locked out; this check is skipped when a `--token` static token is configured); create another one first.

Also: a static token given with `--token` / `$MUSIC_API_TOKEN` at server start is accepted too, but it is not listed and can't be revoked through the API.

### System audio (the host machine's mixer, not Spotify)

#### GET /api/system/volume
`{"backend": "macos"|"pipewire"|"pulseaudio", "volume": 0-100, "muted": bool}`. This is the computer's output volume, separate from Spotify's volume.

#### POST /api/system/volume
Body `{volume?: 0-100, delta?: ±n, muted?: bool}`. Returns the new state.

#### GET /api/system/outputs
Audio outputs on Linux (PipeWire/PulseAudio): `[{"id", "name", "default", ...}]`. `501` on macOS.

#### POST /api/system/outputs
Body `{id}`: make that output the default (Linux only, `501` elsewhere).

### Spotify passthrough

#### ANY /api/spotify/{path}
Forwards the request to `https://api.spotify.com/v1/{path}` with the server's Spotify login: same method, query string (minus `token`), and JSON body if one is sent. Returns `{"result": <Spotify's raw JSON, or null>}`. Use it for anything not wrapped above, e.g. `GET /api/spotify/me/player/devices` or `GET /api/spotify/playlists/{id}?fields=name,owner`. Spotify's development-mode limits (section 6) still apply.

### Spotify login (Web API)

#### GET /auth
`{"result": {"configured", "logged_in", "scope", "redirect_uri", "expires_at"}}`. Check `logged_in` before relying on Web API endpoints.

#### GET /auth/login
HTML login page for a human (open in a browser with `?token=...`). `?redirect=1` sends `302` straight to Spotify. The page also has a box for the paste flow.

#### GET /auth/callback
OAuth redirect target. No API token; protected by the PKCE `state`.

#### POST /auth/paste
Body `{url}`: the full URL Spotify redirected to (`...?code=...&state=...`). Finishes login when the redirect couldn't load (e.g. it points at `127.0.0.1` on another machine). Returns the login status.

#### POST /auth/logout
Forget the stored Spotify login. Returns the login status. Don't call this unless the user asks; logging back in needs a human with a browser.

### Documentation (no token)

`GET /llms.txt`, `GET /llms-full.txt` (this file), `GET /LLMS.md` (same as this file), `GET /API.md` (endpoint table), `GET /README.md`, and `GET /` (web remote for people).

---

## 4. Server-sent events

`GET /api/events?token=...` (or with the Authorization header) streams `text/event-stream`:

| Event | Data | When |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | status object | Right after connecting (if known), then every 1 s (Soloist) or 2 s (connect), and immediately on Soloist push events |
| `track` | track/episode object or `null` | When the current item changes |
| `queue` | `{upcoming, previous}` | When the queue changes (Soloist backend only) |
| `sleep` | sleep status | When a sleep timer is set, cancelled or fires |
| `activity` | activity entry | When someone does something (see `GET /api/activity`). A coalesced or name-enriched entry is sent again with the same `id` |
| `error` | `{"error": "..."}` | When fetching status fails (e.g. Spotify unreachable) |

Lines starting with `:` (`: ping`) are keep-alives sent after 15 s of silence. Status polling only runs while at least one client is subscribed.

```sh
curl -sN "$API/api/events?token=$TOKEN"
```

```js
const es = new EventSource(`${API}/api/events?token=${TOKEN}`);
es.addEventListener("status", e => console.log(JSON.parse(e.data).track?.name));
```

For one-off questions ("what's playing?") use `GET /api/status` instead.

---

## 5. Workflows

### Find and play a song

1. `GET /api/search?q=<words>&type=track&limit=5`
2. Pick the best match from `result.tracks.items` (check `name` and `artists[].name`; if the user named an artist, put it in `q`, e.g. `q=track:Clocks artist:Coldplay`).
3. `POST /api/play {"uri": "<track uri>"}`. The response is the new status; confirm `track.name`.
4. If it fails with a 404 mentioning no active device (connect backend): `GET /api/devices`, then `POST /api/devices/transfer {"device": "<name or id>", "play": false}`, and retry step 3. If `/api/devices` is empty, no Spotify app is open on the account; a human has to open one.

To play an album, playlist, artist or podcast, search with that `type` and `POST /api/play {"uri": "<its uri>"}`. To start a playlist at a particular song: `POST /api/play {"context": "<playlist uri>", "offset": "<track uri>"}` or `POST /api/playlists/{id}/play {"offset": 4}`.

### Play something next without interrupting

`POST /api/queue {"uri": "<track uri>"}`. Then `POST /api/next` if the user wants it now.

### Add the current song to a playlist

1. `GET /api/now-playing` and take `uri` (null means nothing is playing).
2. `GET /api/playlists?limit=50` and find the playlist by `name` (page with `offset` if `next` is true). Only playlists the user owns (`owner` equals `GET /api/me` `name`) or that are `collaborative` can be edited.
3. `POST /api/playlists/{id}/items {"uris": ["<uri>"]}`.
4. Optionally check for duplicates first: `GET /api/playlists/{id}/items` and compare `uri`s.

If the playlist doesn't exist yet: `POST /api/playlists {"name": "..."}`, then use its `id`.

### Like or unlike the current song

`PATCH /api/tracks/current {"saved": true}` (or `false`). `GET /api/tracks/current` shows `saved`.

### Show lyrics

1. `GET /api/lyrics`.
2. If `instrumental` is true, say so. If `synced` is non-empty, `synced[line].text` is the current line (show a few lines around it); otherwise show `plain`.
3. To follow along live, re-fetch `GET /api/lyrics` (it's cached server-side after the first lookup) or compute the line from `status.position_ms` and `synced[].time_ms` using the `status` SSE event.

### What's playing / what was played

- Now: `GET /api/status` (track, artist, position, device, volume).
- Up next: `GET /api/queue`.
- Earlier: `GET /api/recent?limit=10`.

### Volume and sleep

- Spotify volume: `POST /api/volume {"delta": -10}` or `{"volume": 40}`.
- If Spotify is at 100 and it's still too quiet (or the device doesn't support remote volume), use the computer's mixer: `POST /api/system/volume {"delta": 10}`.
- Stop in 30 minutes with a 1-minute fade: `POST /api/sleep {"minutes": 30, "fade": 60}`.

### Manage tokens

- See who has access: `GET /api/tokens` (your own token has `current: true`).
- Give a new device or person access: `POST /api/tokens {"name": "front-desk iPad"}`, then hand over `result.token` (shown only once). For the web remote, the link `https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org/?token=<token>` signs the browser in.
- Revoke: `DELETE /api/tokens/{id}`. Effective on the next request.
- Rotate your own token: create a new one, switch to it, then `DELETE` the old one by `id` (deleting the token you're using also works, but then your next request is 401).
- `409` on delete means it's the last token; create a replacement first.

### Spotify login missing or expired

If a Web API call fails with 412 and a message pointing at `/auth/login` ("not logged in to the Spotify Web API", "Spotify login expired or was revoked", or "... needs the Spotify Web API"), an agent can't fix it alone. Ask a human to open `https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org/auth/login?token=<token>` in a browser and log in with Spotify. If the redirect lands on an `http://127.0.0.1:8765/auth/callback?...` page that doesn't load, they copy that whole URL into the box on the login page (or send it with `POST /auth/paste {"url": "..."}`).

---

## 6. Limits and gotchas

### Spotify Web API (development-mode app, 2026 rules)

- Search returns at most 10 results per type per request. Page with `offset`, or make `q` more specific.
- Playlist items can only be read for playlists the user owns or collaborates on. Any playlist can still be played by URI, and its details (`GET /api/playlists/{id}`) still work.
- The Spotify app allows at most 5 users, and its owner needs Premium.
- Removed by Spotify and not available here (not even through `/api/spotify/*`): browse/categories, new releases, featured playlists, artist top tracks, recommendations, related artists, audio features/analysis, popularity, and batch lookups of several IDs at once.
- Saving and removing goes through Spotify's generic library endpoint (`PUT/DELETE /api/library`), max 40 URIs per call.
- Spotify rate limits (`429`) are retried once automatically when the wait is 5 s or less; otherwise the 429 is returned.

### Playback backends

The server uses one of two backends; `GET /api/backend` says which.

- `connect`: controls whatever Spotify Connect device is active on the account (Spotify desktop app, phone, speaker) through the Web API. Needs the Web API login, Premium on the account, and a device that is online. With no active device, play commands fail (Spotify 404, "no active device"); transfer to a device first. Status is polled every 2 s while someone listens to events. Previous-queue history isn't available. The public server runs on macOS, where this is normally the backend.
- `soloist`: plays through a local Spotify Soloist daemon (Linux) over its WebSocket API, with push events and no Web API rate limits. Status, transport, volume, shuffle, repeat, seek, queue reading and queueing tracks work without the Web API. These fall back to the Web API (aimed at the Soloist device): playing with `uris`, `context`, `offset` or `position`; playing an artist or show URI; queueing episodes; listing other devices; transferring to another device. The queue includes previous items and up to 80 upcoming, each tagged `context`, `queue` or `autoplay`. `POST /api/backend/soloist/activate` makes it the active device. Soloist errors mentioning auth come back as 409; Soloist not running is 503; no answer is 504.

### Other gotchas

- `uri` in `/api/play` and URIs in library/playlist bodies must be URIs or links; a bare ID there is a 400 ("not a Spotify URI or link"). Path parameters are the opposite: bare IDs only.
- `offset` in `/api/play` is a position if it's a number or a digit string (`3` or `"3"`), otherwise a track URI, link or ID.
- `PUT /api/playlists/{id}/items` with `uris` replaces the whole playlist.
- `DELETE /api/playlists/{id}/items` removes every occurrence of each URI.
- On the connect backend Spotify can take a moment to apply a command, so the status returned right after it may still show the old state. Re-check after a second (or watch the next `status` event).
- `GET /api` isn't wrapped in `{"result": ...}`.
- The sleep timer and lyrics cache live in server memory and reset when the server restarts.
- The server holds a single Spotify login: everything (library, playlists, history) is that one account's.

---

## 7. Errors

| Status | Typical `error` | Meaning / what to do |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad request: 'q'`, `bad request: not a Spotify URI or link: ...`, `bad request: give uris`, `invalid JSON body` | Missing or malformed parameter; fix the request |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or wrong API token |
| 412 | `not logged in to the Spotify Web API; open /auth/login`, `Spotify login expired or was revoked ...` | Server's Spotify login missing or expired; a human must log in (section 5) |
| 403 | `Spotify 403: ...` | Spotify refused: e.g. Premium required, playlist not yours, user not on the app's allowlist |
| 404 | `not found`, `nothing playing`, `no lyrics found`, `device '...' not found`, `Spotify 404: ... (NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE)` | Missing thing; for no active device, transfer playback first |
| 405 | `method not allowed` | Path exists, wrong method |
| 409 | `refusing to revoke the last token ...`, Soloist auth errors | Conflict; see message |
| 412 | `... needs the Spotify Web API; log in at /auth/login`, `no Spotify Client ID ...` | Feature needs the Web API login, which isn't set up |
| 429 | `Spotify 429: ...` | Spotify rate limit; wait and retry |
| 501 | `no supported system mixer ...`, `output switching needs PipeWire or PulseAudio` | Not supported on this host |
| 502 | `Spotify 5xx: ...`, `cannot reach Spotify: ...`, `lrclib: ...` | Upstream failure; retry later |
| 503 / 504 | `Soloist not connected`, `Soloist did not answer ...` | Soloist daemon down or slow |

Other Spotify 4xx errors are passed through with their status and a message of the form `Spotify <code>: <message> (<reason>)`.

---

## 8. Deployment (for maintainers)

- Code: a Python 3.9+ stdlib-only server (`server.py`), installed at `~/.local/share/music-api-v2` on a Raspberry Pi 3 B+ (Debian 13, user `ubuntu`). No dependencies.
- systemd user units: `soloist.service` (Spotify Soloist, audio to the USB speakers via PipeWire), `music-api.service` (`server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --public`, settings from `~/.config/music-api/env`), `soloist-update.timer` (daily build refresh).
- System service `cloudflared` (config `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml`) maps `music.pinewoodrobotics.org` to `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.
- Restart: `systemctl --user restart music-api`. Logs: `journalctl --user-unit soloist --user-unit music-api -f`.
- Data directory `~/.local/share/music-api`: `spotify-tokens.json` (Spotify login), `api-tokens.json` (hashed API tokens), `token` (bootstrap token file).
- First start with auth required and no tokens yet: if `<data-dir>/token` exists (the v1 token was migrated there) it's imported as a token named "v1 token" and the plaintext file is deleted; otherwise a new token is generated and written to `<data-dir>/token` (mode 600) for the admin to read.
- Spotify login through the public URL needs `https://music.pinewoodrobotics.org/auth/callback` listed as a Redirect URI in the Spotify app and the server started with `--redirect-uri` set to it; otherwise use the paste flow.
- v1 (Music.app-based, `~/Developer/music-api`) is retired.
